newsitem.title: USA: Police to help tenants if New York rent laws lapse.
newsitem.headline: Police to help tenants if New York rent laws lapse.

text.p: New York police will crack down on any harassment by landlords if the state lets rent stabilisation laws, which protect more than 2 million tenants from big increases, lapse next week, the mayor said Wednesday.
Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said his orders to police were part of a plan his administration was developing in anticipation of the expiration of the city's rent stabilisation laws Sunday.
He said a special police task force would begin investigating complaints from tenants June 16.

"I trust everyone, but I'll still have a lot of police out there investigating allegations of harassment," Giuliani said at a City Hall press conference. "Some landlords are saying there won't be harassment. That's fine. But there will be other landlords that will harass tenants."

The mayor said the administration would establish at least two hot lines for tenants. One will be a direct line to police for reporting incidents of abuse by landlords. The other will handle general tenant questions and serve as a referral service if callers need the help of lawyers.
Giuliani said he was taking these steps to avoid having "2.4 million people in a state of confusion, fear and upset."

Lewis Rudin, chairman of a group of major landlords who have pledged to abide by the current laws even if they expire Sunday, pledged, "There will be no chaos Monday." His group will work with police to identify abusive landlords, he said.

New York's rent stabilisation laws will expire Sunday unless the New York Legislature enacts an extension. Gov. George Pataki and Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno, both Republicans, have yet to agree on a compromise resolution, with Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver, a Manhattan Democrat.
The laws, which are widely popular with the city's residents, cap rent increases on about 1.2 million apartments.
